title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents

revision_signal: multi-turn online RL with a reward bonus on second-attempt improvement over the first attempt
note: Two-turn self-correction RL with a policy-initialisation phase and an improvement bonus to avoid collapse; +15.6% (MATH) and +9.1% (HumanEval) self-correction on Gemini 1.0 Pro / 1.5 Flash; shows turn-level credit shaping matters.
title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning

belief_level_metrics: proxy: state-based unit tests including collateral-damage checks

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents

revision_signal: outcome reward on final answer from end-to-end RL in live web search; emergent cross-validation and self-reflection
belief_level_metrics: proxy: honesty when evidence is unavailable (qualitative)
note: End-to-end RL with real web search yields up to +28.9 over prompt baselines and +7.2 over RAG-RL agents and emergent planning, cross-source verification and honesty about missing evidence; evidence acquisition trained by trajectory-level credit.
title: DeepResearcher: Scaling Deep Research via Reinforcement Learning in Real-world Environments

revision_signal: doubly-robust step-level advantage mixing Monte-Carlo return with step value TD; instruction-level value drives automatic curriculum
note: Offline-to-online RL for Android GUI control with step-level and instruction-level value functions and a doubly robust advantage estimator; 1.3B VLM rises from 17.7% to 67.2% success on AitW, beating filtered BC (57.8%).
title: DigiRL: Training In-The-Wild Device-Control Agents with Autonomous Reinforcement Learning

revision_signal: none (outcome reward on final answer; simulated retrieval with curriculum-degraded document quality)
note: RL search agent trained against an LLM-simulated search engine; 7B simulator matches and 14B surpasses real search engine; credit is outcome-level over the whole search trajectory, so no per-step or state-level signal.
title: ZeroSearch: Incentivize the Search Capability of LLMs without Searching

revision_signal: subgoal completion judged by the LLM triggers summarisation of the finished chunk; only current-subgoal action-observation pairs retained
belief_level_metrics: proxy: steps to completion and success rate on long-horizon tasks
note: Subgoal-chunked working memory: LLM decides when to replace a completed subgoal's observations with a summary; success doubles (42% vs 21% across Blocksworld/Gripper/Tyreworld/Barman/Jericho) and 3.8 fewer steps on average; no analysis of what the summary loses.
title: HiAgent: Hierarchical Working Memory Management for Solving Long-Horizon Agent Tasks with Large Language Model
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: none (evaluation only; agent has scratchpad, key-value store and vector DB plus 30k-token rolling context)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: days until sales stop; net worth; no explicit belief-accuracy metric
note: Long-horizon coherence benchmark (>20M tokens per run): Claude 3.5 Sonnet mean net worth $2218 vs Gemini 2.0 Pro $274; failures are belief failures (assuming delivery on the emailed arrival date, forgetting orders, meltdown loops) and are not correlated with context-window exhaustion.
title: Vending-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Term Coherence of Autonomous Agents

revision_signal: switching condition: replan when predicted state differs from observation, on unexpected reward, or after repeated failure (theory: posterior entropy drop > log 2)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: regret bound sqrt(T); task success
note: Casts LLM reasoning as learning and planning in a Bayes-adaptive MDP: the memory buffer of transitions is the information state and the LLM is prompted to form an in-context posterior; proves sqrt(T) regret and reports 99% on ALFWorld and 93% on Game of 24; belief is implicit in history, not an explicit object.
title: Reason for Future, Act for Now: A Principled Framework for Autonomous LLM Agents with Provable Sample Efficiency

revision_signal: user-stated add/update/delete of preferences across weeks-to-months of sessions; memory traces track state transitions
belief_level_metrics: yes: FAMA = max(0, memory-presence accuracy - lambda*(1 - forgetting-absence accuracy))
note: Long-term personalised-memory benchmark whose FAMA metric explicitly penalises reliance on invalidated memories; six memory agents (A-Mem, LangMem, Mem0, MemoBase, MemoryOS, Nemori) still reuse obsolete memories and reasoning over memory stays near 28%.
title: From Recall to Forgetting: Benchmarking Long-Term Memory for Personalized Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: inference-time: intention-aware hierarchical world model anticipates future tool calls and risk-calibrated cost; replanned online per step
belief_level_metrics: proxy: budget feasibility and task success under price shifts
note: Budget-constrained tool agent that plans over a learned intention-aware hierarchical world model in context space; enforces hard budget feasibility on cost-augmented StableToolBench and stays robust to tool price changes.
title: Budget-Constrained Agentic Large Language Models: Intention-Based Planning for Costly Tool Use

revision_signal: retrospective reflection over the executed trajectory plus a latent world model; double-loop policy adaptation on detected drift
belief_level_metrics: yes: Semantic Fidelity Index (SFI) and drift contraction coefficient alpha
note: Models long-horizon Semantic-Execution Drift as a stochastic recurrence D(t+1)=alpha D(t)+eps+beta P(t); ReflectiChain reaches SFI 88.7 with alpha=0.823 on the 30-step Sema-Sim supply-chain benchmark, reflection contributing most (abstract only; no arXiv id).
title: ReflectiChain: Mitigating Semantic-Execution Drift in Long-Horizon LLM Agents via Retrospective Reflection and Double-Loop Policy Adaptation

revision_signal: world model conditions on state anchors (tool schemas, prior turns, expected outcomes); GRPO agent training with deterministic state checks
belief_level_metrics: proxy: coherence, groundedness and rollout diversity of simulated states; human realism judgements
note: Masked-diffusion text world models trained on 239k state-action trajectories beat autoregressive models 4x larger on state coherence and groundedness; agents trained with GRPO inside the world model gain up to 47% absolute on ScienceWorld/ALFWorld/AppWorld zero-shot.
title: Masked Diffusion Language Models are Strong and Steerable Text-Based World Models for Agentic RL

revision_signal: reasoning traces used to induce, track and update the plan; actions fetch external evidence
note: Foundational interleaved reason-act loop: reasoning traces track and update plans while actions gather evidence; +34% ALFWorld and +10% WebShop success over imitation/RL baselines; the belief lives only in the growing context.
title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

revision_signal: reflector extracts lessons from execution feedback; curator applies structured incremental updates to the playbook (avoids context collapse from full rewrites)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: task success after context adaptation; context-collapse case study
note: Treats the context as an evolving playbook updated by generator-reflector-curator; names brevity bias and context collapse as failure modes of iterative rewriting; +10.6% on agent benchmarks and matches the top AppWorld agent with a smaller open model, using execution feedback without labels.
title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models

revision_signal: self-judged success/failure of each task distils strategies that are written back; memory-aware test-time scaling yields contrastive experiences
belief_level_metrics: proxy: task success and step efficiency across tasks
note: Memory of distilled reasoning strategies from both successful and failed self-judged experiences beats raw-trajectory and success-only memories on WebArena/Mind2Web/SWE-Bench-Verified; MaTTS scales memory quality with interaction compute.
title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory

revision_signal: online semantic synthesis merges related context intra-session; intent-aware retrieval planning sets scope
belief_level_metrics: proxy: LoCoMo F1 and token cost
note: Semantic lossless-compression memory pipeline; +26.4% average F1 on LoCoMo with up to 30x fewer inference tokens; conversational memory with no uncertainty condition.
title: SimpleMem: Efficient Lifelong Memory for LLM Agents

revision_signal: dialogue-chain FIFO from short- to mid-term and segmented-page promotion to long-term personal memory
note: OS-inspired three-tier memory with explicit update rules; +49.11% F1 and +46.18% BLEU-1 on LoCoMo with GPT-4o-mini; later shown by Memora to still reuse invalidated memories.
title: Memory OS of AI Agent
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

revision_signal: none
note: Neighbouring survey organised around what/when/how to evolve (models, memory, tools, architecture); covers memory evolution and textual-feedback signals but does not treat belief state or credited object as the organising question.
title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence

revision_signal: addition gated by trajectory evaluators; deletion by frequency thresholds or history-based utility from downstream task outcomes
belief_level_metrics: proxy: input-output similarity correlation; error rate of retained vs deleted records
note: Shows LLM agents follow retrieved experiences almost verbatim (Pearson r near 1), so noisy memory records propagate errors and seemingly correct records mislead; strict addition evaluators lift EHRAgent from 26.19% to 34.66% and history-based deletion to 42.06% while cutting memory 75%; downstream task outcomes act as free credit for memory records.
title: How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: none
belief_level_metrics: proxy: belief-attribution accuracy on 8 ToM tasks / 31 abilities
note: Bilingual multiple-choice ToM benchmark; GPT-4 trails humans by >10 points; single-turn other-agent belief attribution, cited for the ToM lineage only.
title: ToMBench: Benchmarking Theory of Mind in Large Language Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: cross-task experience replay; group self-consistency over retrieved experiences
belief_level_metrics: proxy: lifelong success across skill-dependent tasks
note: Lifelong-learning benchmark over Database/OS/Knowledge-Graph environments; plain experience replay helps little because of irrelevant records and context limits; group self-consistency improves it.
title: LifelongAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners

revision_signal: new partial observations during active exploration; false-belief paradigm relocates four objects after initial exploration
belief_level_metrics: yes: cognitive-map positional, directional and facing accuracy; stability over time; change identification rate
note: Benchmark that probes an explicit JSON spatial belief at every step: Active-Passive Gap (GPT-5.2 57.1% passive to 46.0% active), belief instability over time, and Belief Inertia where vision agents identify only 14.4% of orientation changes (Gemini-3 Pro) versus 98.7% in text.
title: Theory of Space: Can Foundation Models Construct Spatial Beliefs through Active Exploration?

revision_signal: render-aware RL rewards rendered next-screen fidelity and action consistency
belief_level_metrics: proxy: next-UI prediction quality; downstream navigation success
note: GUI world model that predicts the next screen as renderable HTML; Code2World-8B rivals GPT-5 on next-UI prediction and adds +9.5% AndroidWorld success to Gemini-2.5-Flash when used for foresight.
title: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation

revision_signal: trained on 1M+ open-web interactions; used for synthetic trajectories and inference-time search
note: Open-web simulator matching Gemini-3-Pro on simulation quality; Qwen3-14B trained on its synthetic trajectories gains +9.2% on WebArena and it outperforms GPT-5 as an inference-time world model.
title: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training

revision_signal: DDT stage 1 trains state prediction / state-difference / critique of own simulations vs observed next state; stage 2 trajectory-level outcome reward R=1/0
belief_level_metrics: yes: GPT-4o-judged world-model simulation accuracy (55.7% with critique training vs 38.9%; r=0.44 with task success)
note: Trains the agent's internal world-model simulation as an auxiliary objective before policy training; critique-of-simulation is the most effective signal, WindowsAgentArena 34.9% vs 20.9%, OSWorld 44.3 best-of-n matching R1 with 2x fewer tokens; better world modelling correlates with better agents.
title: Dyna-Think: Synergizing Reasoning, Acting, and World Model Simulation in AI Agents

revision_signal: testing-team unit tests and simulation-based validation give behaviour-level feedback on generated PDDL/executable world models
belief_level_metrics: proxy: world-model validity on three PDDL/code benchmarks
note: Multi-agent pipeline generating executable symbolic world models with adaptive testing feedback; SFT on the resulting multi-turn trajectories yields +30.95% relative gain; the world model is an explicit object but credit is trajectory-level.
title: Agent2World: Learning to Generate Symbolic World Models via Adaptive Multi-Agent Feedback

revision_signal: none
note: Foundational output-level credit: closed-form policy from preference pairs with a classification loss; defines the 'credit to output' baseline that multi-turn agent methods extend to trajectory/state.
title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

revision_signal: self-assessed retrieval need (reflection tokens: Retrieve/IsRel/IsSup/IsUse)
note: Single LM learns to decide when evidence is needed and to critique retrieved passages via reflection tokens; 7B/13B outperform ChatGPT on open-domain QA and fact verification. Lineage for evidence-acquisition-on-demand, but single-turn.
title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

revision_signal: edited fact stored externally; iterative prompting checks generated answers against stored edits
belief_level_metrics: yes: multi-hop accuracy after edit (ripple-effect consistency)
note: Editing one fact should ripple to entailed beliefs: current editors recall the edited fact but fail catastrophically on multi-hop questions; MeLLo (external edit memory + iterative consistency prompting) outperforms them by a large margin. Lineage for belief-revision consistency failure modes.
title: MQuAKE: Assessing Knowledge Editing in Language Models via Multi-Hop Questions
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

revision_signal: TD-loss update of a learned belief network over co-agent strategies (belief embedding from local history)
note: Recasts multi-LLM coordination as an incomplete-information game: each execution LLM keeps a belief-state embedding about co-agents (trained by TD loss) and receives an individual trajectory-level reward (action-likelihood + task + collaborative contribution); +11.2% over debate on six benchmarks with 21.4% fewer tokens. Belief is over other agents, not the environment.
title: From Debate to Equilibrium: Belief-Driven Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning via Bayesian Nash Equilibrium

revision_signal: in-context evidence pieces presented within conversation history
belief_level_metrics: yes: Bayesian Coherence Coefficient (correlation of expected vs observed log-odds updates)
note: Defines BCC = Corr(expected LLR update, observed log-odds change) on 6,460 (class pair, evidence, history) tuples; BCC correlates with log parameter count at r=0.906 across five model families, all models > 0. A belief-level revision metric in context, without an acting agent.
title: Are LLM Belief Updates Consistent with Bayes' Theorem?
evidence: P (ICML 2025 Workshop on Assessing World Models)

revision_signal: none (evaluation only)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: transition-modeling F1 on predicted preconditions/effects and planner success; error taxonomy (hallucination, affordance, planning)
note: Formalizes four LLM modules incl. transition modeling (predict PDDL preconditions/effects) with logic-matching F1 and planner success; Claude-3.5 gets 78.8% F1 on object states but 58.6% on spatial relations, o1-preview 90.2% planner success on BEHAVIOR; LLMs overstate effects and understate preconditions. A benchmark of the agent's world model.
title: Embodied Agent Interface: Benchmarking LLMs for Embodied Decision Making

revision_signal: user preference stated explicitly or implicitly earlier in conversation
belief_level_metrics: proxy: preference-following accuracy over turns (memory validity of user state)
note: 3,000 preference/query pairs over 20 topics in multi-session conversations up to 100k tokens; zero-shot preference following drops below 10% at just 10 turns (~3k tokens) for most of 10 models, RAG and prompting still degrade with length, fine-tuning helps. Measures persistence of a user-state claim across decisions.
title: Do LLMs Recognize Your Preferences? Evaluating Personalized Preference Following in LLMs

revision_signal: memory lifecycle scheduling: MemCubes with provenance and versioning composed, migrated, fused over time
note: Treats memory as an OS-managed resource unifying plaintext, activation and parameter memories in versioned MemCubes with provenance; a representation-level proposal for memory evolution, without belief-level evaluation in the abstract.
title: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System

revision_signal: none (evaluation only)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: memory effectiveness, efficiency and capacity across factual vs reflective memory levels
note: Benchmark of LLM-agent memory with factual and reflective levels and participation vs observation scenarios, scored on effectiveness, efficiency and capacity; no headline numbers in abstract.
title: MemBench: Towards More Comprehensive Evaluation on the Memory of LLM-based Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: none (state is screenshot history in context)
note: Asynchronous distributed online RL for Android control with A-RIDE: sparse AI-evaluator terminal reward plus step penalties, step-level advantages from a value classifier with trajectory-level filtering and Retrace(lambda) off-policy correction; 3x training efficiency and 73.2% vs 61.2% success over DigiRL. Credit flows to trajectory/steps, not to state.
title: DistRL: An Asynchronous Distributed Reinforcement Learning Framework for On-Device Control Agents

revision_signal: LLM emits memory-write of extracted triplets; updatable, aggregatable store queried on demand
note: Early explicit read-write triplet memory unit for LLMs (Davidsonian triplets), updatable and interpretable, with qualitative gains on temporal QA; lineage for written external memory. Credit: imitation of memory API calls only.
title: RET-LLM: Towards a General Read-Write Memory for Large Language Models

revision_signal: accumulated simulated user feedback during service time
belief_level_metrics: proxy: continual-learning gains from accumulated feedback (effectiveness and efficiency)
note: User-feedback simulation framework and multi-domain, multilingual benchmark for memory and continual learning in LLM systems; SOTA memory baselines are 'far from satisfying' at learning from service-time feedback.
title: MemoryBench: A Benchmark for Memory and Continual Learning in LLM Systems

revision_signal: internal activation belief shift during CoT (probe-detected)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: activation-probe answer decodability vs CoT-monitor detection; token savings from probe-guided early exit
note: Activation probes decode the model's committed answer far earlier than a CoT monitor can, exposing a belief-vs-verbalisation gap; probe-guided early exit cuts tokens up to 80% (MMLU) and 30% (GPQA-Diamond) at similar accuracy. Single-turn only, but a clean instance of the belief-report gap the survey discusses.
title: Reasoning Theater: Disentangling Model Beliefs from Chain-of-Thought

revision_signal: per-step human process labels (PRM800K)
note: Process supervision beats outcome supervision on MATH (78% of a test subset); the canonical step-level credit-assignment reference from which agent PRMs descend. Single-turn math, cited for lineage.
title: Let's Verify Step by Step

revision_signal: none (browsing history in context; reward from human preference on final answer)
note: Behaviour cloning + rejection sampling against a preference RM on a multi-step browsing environment; answers preferred over human demonstrators 56%. Early example of outcome-level credit for an interactive information-seeking agent.
title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

revision_signal: user pushback / stated user view (social pressure) flips the model's answer
belief_level_metrics: proxy: rate of answer change under user disagreement; preference-model preference for sycophantic responses
note: Five assistants consistently abandon correct answers to match user views; human preference data and PMs prefer sycophantic responses a non-negligible fraction of the time, so RLHF itself induces unwarranted belief revision. Key evidence for the 'revision without evidence' failure mode.
title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models

revision_signal: automatic per-step labels via MC completion rollouts
note: Automatically constructed process reward model; step-wise PPO lifts Mistral-7B GSM8K 77.9%->84.1%, MATH 28.6%->33.0%. Lineage for label-free step-level credit that agent PRMs adapt.
title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: none (search results appended to context; outcome reward on final answer)
note: Two-stage outcome-only RL (no process reward, no distillation cold start) teaches the LLM to invoke search mid-reasoning; beats strong RAG baselines including GPT-4o-mini. Evidence-acquisition policy learned with purely outcome-level credit.
title: R1-Searcher: Incentivizing the Search Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

revision_signal: outer-loop search over harness code using scores and execution traces of prior candidates
note: Outer loop searches over the harness code that decides what to store/retrieve/present; beats a SOTA context-management system by 7.7 points with 4x fewer context tokens and improves IMO-level RAG math by 4.7 points across five held-out models. Treats memory policy as the object of optimisation rather than the model.
title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses

revision_signal: none (egocentric observations in context; RL on task reward)
note: Frozen LLM adapted as an RL policy from environment interaction alone; 42% success on 1,000 unseen Language Rearrangement tasks, 1.7x baselines. Example of trajectory-level credit with an implicit (in-context) state.
title: Large Language Models as Generalizable Policies for Embodied Tasks

revision_signal: controller selects extract/consolidate/prune skills per trace; designer revises skill set from hard cases
belief_level_metrics: proxy: downstream QA/task accuracy on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, HotpotQA, ALFWorld
note: Reframes memory extraction/consolidation/pruning as learnable, evolving skills with a trained controller and a designer that revises the skill set from failure cases; improves over strong baselines across four memory/agent benchmarks (numbers not in abstract). Directly credits the memory operation.
title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents

revision_signal: self-curation after each query: model writes/edits reusable strategy snippets without labels
belief_level_metrics: proxy: accuracy gain from persistent memory across queries
note: Black-box LM given a persistent self-curated cheatsheet; GPT-4o Game of 24 10%->99%, Claude AIME accuracy more than doubled, +9% GPQA-Diamond. Test-time memory that persists across episodes, curated by the model itself.
title: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: none (SFT on decomposed agent corpora; negative samples for hallucination)
note: Redesigns agent SFT corpora and adds negative samples; Llama2-7B beats prior best by 3.5% on agent benchmarks and reduces agent hallucination. Trajectory-level supervised credit; the hallucination benchmark is a proxy for ungrounded state.
title: Agent-FLAN: Designing Data and Methods of Effective Agent Tuning for Large Language Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

revision_signal: graph updater infers and updates latent belief graph each step, trained with self-supervision plus RL
belief_level_metrics: proxy: policy performance and generalisation from learned graph vs text-only
note: Pre-LLM lineage: transformer agent learns to infer and update a latent belief graph of a text game, trained with RL plus self-supervision; +24.2% over text-only baselines on 500+ TextWorld games. Direct ancestor of explicit-state agents with a state-level learning signal.
title: Learning Dynamic Belief Graphs to Generalize on Text-Based Games

revision_signal: peer arguments in multi-agent debate rounds
belief_level_metrics: proxy: belief-trajectory martingale analysis; correctness after debate vs voting
note: Models multi-agent debate as a stochastic process and proves agents' belief trajectories form a martingale, so debate alone does not raise expected correctness; majority voting explains most of MAD's gains, and interventions biasing updates toward correction help. Theoretical result on when belief revision from peers is uninformative.
title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?

revision_signal: ToM-style belief inference over the agent's trajectory flags misaligned actions before execution; user alert triggers correction
note: Uses LLM belief reasoning (Theory-of-Mind) to infer user intent from the agent's trajectory and pre-emptively detect misaligned critical actions; up to 20% Marco-F1 improvement over baselines on three agent tasks. Belief about the user drives a gate on action.
title: Preemptive Detection and Correction of Misaligned Actions in LLM Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

revision_signal: Bayesian belief updating plus noisy replicator dynamics from payoff feedback each round
belief_level_metrics: proxy: emergence and stability of cooperation over rounds
note: LLM agents in a multi-person Prisoner's Dilemma update Bayesian beliefs about others from payoff history; cooperation emerges and stabilises with individual heterogeneity. Off-core application but a concrete external-filter belief architecture; abstract only.
title: A Large Language Model-Enabled Framework for Simulating Multi-Agent Cooperative Game

revision_signal: new text knowledge injected into latent memory pool (self-update)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: knowledge retention after sequential updates and model-editing accuracy
note: Fixed-size latent memory pool self-updates with new text and retains injected knowledge without degradation after nearly a million updates; latent-parametric alternative to written memory.
title: MEMORYLLM: Towards Self-Updatable Large Language Models

revision_signal: new user information across turns (models fail to revise early assumptions)
belief_level_metrics: proxy: aptitude vs unreliability decomposition of single- vs multi-turn gap
note: Across 200k+ simulated conversations all tested LLMs drop 39% on average from single- to multi-turn; they commit to early assumptions and do not recover, a documented belief-revision failure mode.
title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation

revision_signal: none (offline returns from logged dialogues)
note: Offline implicit Q-learning for LMs learns conservative value functions from logged data to steer generation in end-to-end multi-turn dialogue; foundational offline-RL credit signal for language agents.
title: Offline RL for Natural Language Generation with Implicit Language Q Learning

revision_signal: belief-update objective (SLAG) applied to parametric beliefs with consistency constraints
belief_level_metrics: yes: logical consistency of updated beliefs; belief graph
note: Frames LM factual claims as beliefs; introduces consistency metrics for belief updating and SLAG learned optimizers that fix wrong beliefs and improve consistency; lineage for the term belief in LMs (parametric not agentic).
title: Do Language Models Have Beliefs? Methods for Detecting, Updating, and Visualizing Model Beliefs

revision_signal: environment feedback (illegal-move errors) drives iterative code refinement of the harness
note: Gemini-2.5-Flash synthesises a code harness that tracks game state and blocks all illegal moves across 145 TextArena games; code-as-state lets the small model beat Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-5.2-High on 16 one-player games.
title: AutoHarness: improving LLM agents by automatically synthesizing a code harness

revision_signal: alpha-Curriculum Reward aligns simulator-generated task difficulty with agent success
note: Co-evolving generative environment simulator acts as curriculum for agent RL; up to +40.3% over 7B baselines on ALFWorld/API-Bank/BFCL/Bamboogle/TravelPlanner with 3.3x less data; the world model sits on the environment side not the agent.
title: GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators

revision_signal: new evidence across iterative reasoning steps; measures whether updates are predictable from current belief
belief_level_metrics: yes: Martingale Score (regression of belief update on current belief)
note: Unsupervised metric for Bayesian rationality of belief updating in iterative LLM reasoning; finds widespread belief entrenchment (current belief predicts future updates) across models and domains and the score predicts ground-truth accuracy.
title: Martingale Score: An Unsupervised Metric for Bayesian Rationality in LLM Reasoning
